source.title: Alternate Preference Optimization for Unlearning Factual Knowledge in Large Language Models
source.authors: Anmol Reddy Mekala; Vineeth Dorna; Shreya Dubey; Abhishek Lalwani; David Koleczek; Mukund Rungta; Sadid A. Hasan; Elita A. Lobo

record.tranche_reason: The study tests unlearning outcomes using TOFU forgetting and utility metrics, but does not test recovery attacks such as relearning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports forgetting-quality and model-utility results for unlearning methods. These bear on whether unlearning reduces targeted knowledge while retaining general performance, but the paper does not apply recovery attacks. FU and CI assess response coherence and cleanness, not recovery of the targeted knowledge through the attacks named in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study measures TOFU Forget Quality and Model Utility after several unlearning methods on Llama2-7b and Llama3.2-3B. This bears on the first half of A: forgetting while keeping general ability. It runs no recovery attack, so the 'simple attacks don't recover it' half of A, and versions B–F, are untested. AltPO is a new method but makes no robustness-to-attack claim, so it is not F.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that AltPO, which adds in-domain positive feedback via alternate answers, unlearns more stably and effectively, keeping utility and coherence where negative-only methods do not. They also introduce the FU and CI metrics, arguing existing TOFU metrics miss incoherent outputs. They do not test recovery of forgotten knowledge.
record.recipe_differences: AltPO combines negative feedback on forgotten answers with positive preference feedback on multiple plausible alternative answers, plus retain-set feedback; it is evaluated as an unlearning method, not as a recovery attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with the unlearning method, forget-set split, and model. The paper also varies the number of alternate answers and reports different forgetting outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Negative-feedback-only methods (NPO, GradDiff, IdkPO) pass FQ but produce gibberish or inconsistent text on forget prompts. AltPO gives low FU/CI damage on Llama2, but its CI on Llama3.2 is 2.8e-05.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning that passes knowledge-forgetting metrics can still leave detectable, degenerate behaviour on forget prompts.

record.problems: The experiments use TOFU factual QA data and are concentrated on Llama2 and one Llama3.2 setting. Forgetting is assessed with TOFU's statistical FQ measure rather than direct attack recovery; no recovery attack is run.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix Tables 8-11 repeat some main-table results; those duplicate reports are not separate rows. FU/CI and training-trajectory plots are not recorded because they measure response quality or cleanness rather than recovery of targeted knowledge. Ablation results in Tables 2, 3, and 12 are not included as separate rows.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (relearning, prompting, quantization, probing) recover the forgotten TOFU facts after any method, including AltPO.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack.
No activation ablation, probing or analysis of blocking vs deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
AltPO is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for this phenomenon. FQ is a KS test of truth-ratio indistinguishability from the retain model, not accuracy-to-chance. The ablations (Tables 3/12, declared left out) show AltPO's FQ depends on the number of alternates: 0.06 at M=1, 0.74 at M=5, 0.25 at M=10. The rows for the 10% Llama2 split duplicate Table 1.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures forgetting and utility, but does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery attack.
AltPO is proposed as an unlearning method, but the study does not test whether it resists the recovery attacks in the claim.

relationships.condition: AltPO on Llama2-7b (TOFU 1/5/10%) and Llama3.2-3B (10%); NPO on all settings; IdkPO on Llama2
relationships.reason: FQ p-values exceed 0.05 while MU stays near the finetuned reference (r13-r14, r27-r28, r41-r42, r55-r56, r09-r10, r23-r24, r51-r52, r11-r12, r25-r26). Forgetting is measured without attacks.
relationships.display_finding: Forget-quality p-values exceeded 0.05 while model utility remained near the finetuned reference, without recovery attacks.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: AltPO on Llama2-7b (TOFU 1/5/10%) and Llama3.2-3B (10%); NPO on all settings; IdkPO on Llama2
source_check.reason: In the cited rows FQ exceeds 0.05 and MU stays near the finetuned model (Tables 8-11). No attacks were run, so the verdict covers only forgetting with utility. The condition text is too broad: NPO and IdkPO at the 1% split belong to l1 (rows r37-r40), not here.

relationships.condition: Gradient Ascent, GradDiff, and IdkPO on Llama3.2; the 1% split for several baselines
relationships.reason: In these settings either forgetting fails or utility drops. GA: FQ < 0.05 at 5/10% or MU collapses (0.13, 0.00). GradDiff: FQ < 0.05 at 5/10%. IdkPO on Llama3.2: FQ 9e-3. At 1%, GA/GradDiff/NPO/IdkPO lose utility (MU 0.52-0.57).
relationships.display_finding: GA and GradDiff had FQ below 0.05 at 5/10% forgetting, GA utility could collapse to 0.13 or 0.00, and Llama3.2 IdkPO had FQ of 0.009, while at 1% forgetting GA, GradDiff, NPO, and IdkPO had MU of 0.52–0.57.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Gradient Ascent, GradDiff, and IdkPO on Llama3.2; the 1% split for several baselines
source_check.reason: The tables show failures. GA FQ is below 0.05 at 5% and 10%, and its MU collapses (0.13 at 5%, 0.00 on Llama3.2). GradDiff FQ is below 0.05. IdkPO on Llama3.2 has FQ 9.0e-3. At 1% on Llama2, GA, GradDiff, NPO and IdkPO have MU 0.52-0.57 against 0.62. These failures depend on the method, so this is limits_scope, not challenges.

relation.reason: Its results bear on the forgetting-with-utility half of version A.

tranche.reason: AltPO is a different unlearning method aimed at the same question: forgetting while keeping utility. It runs no recovery attacks.

source_check.notes: All 25 rows match Tables 8-11; the Llama2 values also match main Table 1. In the text each caption sits below its table's data. The study tests only the forgetting-with-utility half of A, by TOFU KS-test FQ (not accuracy against chance) and MU. It runs no recovery attack, so B-F are untested. The l0 condition text overlaps l1 at the 1% split.

statements.correction: Llama2-7b-chat (TOFU-finetuned), TOFU 10%, 3 seeds: AltPO FQ 0.74 ± 0.10 (KS-test p-value against the retain model; above 0.05 counts as success). MU 0.62 ± 6.6e-03 against finetuned 0.62. No recovery attack was run.
statements.problem: No error. The statement gives no numbers for this study and names it in neither 'what' nor 'why'; it cites only r13. Its general claim fits r13 and r14: TOFU facts brought to retain-model level, utility kept, Llama 7B, no attack.
